critic_text:
T3 is not correctly bounded. AC3’s keep rule is “whatever Phase 1/2 contributed that no upstream stage produces.” That is an inventory with no inventory. The prompt-file line in T3 does not close it: it is labelled “the candidate,” not the keep set, so any Phase 1/2 leftover (file-order, risk list, test strategy, context pack, complexity branching) can be retained by the same uniqueness claim. That is the original creep in a smaller shape. A closed T3 would be a keep/drop table of current Phase 1/2 outputs against `PIPELINE.md` producers, with anything “better than upstream” recorded and left per the non-goal, not kept. The prompt-file carve-out is right only if that table shows no upstream producer; the spec assumes that instead of requiring the check.

AC3 is not falsifiable as a keep/drop rule. “Kept text names the upstream artifact it supplements” has a cosmetic failing case (missing citation) and no failing case for a keep that should have been a drop. It also contradicts itself: a unique contribution has no upstream artifact to name, and the prompt file is offered as the example of uniqueness. An implementer can satisfy AC3 by adding a sentence or by keeping everything and calling it unique. What would make it an AC: an enumerated keep set, each row either “drop” or “keep, supplements `<artifact>`,” with “no supplement” allowed only for rows in that table.

T1 is an undecided spec. `--human` means a person answers gates on this unit; it does not mean the spec can omit the invocation contract. `--complexity` is already decided by AC4/T2 (read `status.yml`, never re-derive); leaving keep-or-delete open lets T1 restore the finding T2 exists to kill, unless the spec states a precedence exception. `--include-subtasks` is a ticket-path concept; keeping it without AC1’s “optional field” rule reopens finding 3. `--resume` is the one flag that can wait, and only if the spec says mid-stage resume still applies to the phases that stay. Decide each flag in the spec. What would change my mind: an explicit per-flag keep/delete with `--complexity` reconciled to AC4.

AC7 mixes two jobs. “`tasks.md` is the plan” is this stage’s reconciliation and belongs here. “Refuse a unit whose tasks do not map to acceptance criteria” is the claim the preconditions already make and that the scope-audit stage is for; the non-goal says a better-than-upstream check is recorded and left. T6 then weakens it again: AC8 says e2e asserts AC7, T6 only asserts that the file names `tasks.md` as the plan. The mapping refuse is either an unasserted guarantee (Article 3) or out of scope. In-scope remainder: assert the document names `tasks.md` as the plan and that the stage does not invent a second plan. Mapping enforcement stays upstream unless this stage’s preconditions are being asserted as prose, not reimplemented.

Finding 6/7 is Article 2, and scoping the rename to this file is the right bound. Non-goals already send the other ~30 names to a separate sweep. This unit may close without that sweep. It may not close as if Article 2 is satisfied. AC6 is a file-local claim; treat it as one.

All nine listed items are real defects in this file. Finding 7 is a profile hole more than a `PIPELINE.md` contradiction; still real. Missed by the nine, and by the tasks: (a) frontmatter/preconditions were already updated, but T1 rewrites frontmatter as if it were dirty and never carries AC1’s “ticket key remains an optional field”; (b) dropping Phases 1–2 does not say whether remaining phases and the `--human` per-phase gates are renumbered or left with a hole; (c) AC8 asserts AC1/AC2/AC7 only, so AC3–AC6 are guarantees with no assertion, which Article 3 forbids even when they are “checkable by reading.”

- severity: blocker — T3/AC3 keep-whatever is unbounded and self-contradictory (unique work cannot name a supplement); the prompt-file “candidate” is not a closed keep set
- severity: major — T1 defers keep-or-delete of --complexity/--resume/--include-subtasks; keeping --complexity collides with AC4
- severity: major — AC7’s refuse-unmapped-tasks is upstream/precondition work; T6 asserts only “tasks.md is named as the plan” while AC8 cites full AC7
- severity: major — AC8 leaves AC3–AC6 unasserted, so those guarantees are sentences, which Article 3 forbids
- severity: minor — one-file Article 2 fix is correctly bounded; this unit must not close as if the article is cleared
- severity: minor — T1 rewrites already-updated frontmatter and drops AC1’s optional ticket-key remnant
- severity: minor — removing Phases 1–2 does not specify phase renumbering or the --human gate count for what remains
verdict: concerns

The scope is not ready to execute.

T3 is under-bounded: “whatever they contributed” permits reintroducing arbitrary fetch/plan behavior. The prompt-file carve-out is not automatically valid; it needs an explicit purpose, lifecycle, path, and acceptance criterion.

AC3 is not falsifiable. “Names the upstream artifact it supplements” has no defined artifact inventory or test for completeness. Require a closed disposition table for every removed behavior.

T1 is an undecided spec. The fate of `--complexity`, `--resume`, and `--include-subtasks` must be decided before implementation; “decide per flag” merely delegates requirements work to execution.

AC7 is partly appropriate here because task validation is this stage’s precondition, but it is underspecified. Define “maps to acceptance criteria,” the refusal condition, and whether validation is prose-only or an executable assertion. T6 currently tests only that `tasks.md` is named, not that mapping or refusal exists.

AC6 and T5 conflict: AC6 requires a stated durable home for a null tracker, while T5 allows an artifact to be transient. Choose committed repository storage or explicitly declare loss of durability acceptable.

Finding 6/7 can be fixed in this file without violating scope: Article 2 applies to each tracked file, not necessarily one sweep. However, this unit must not claim repository-wide compliance while ~30 other files remain nonconforming; those files are a legitimate separate sweep.

The requirements also miss an Article 3 gap. AC3–AC6 state behavioral guarantees, but AC8 requires executable assertions only for AC1, AC2, and AC7. Either add assertions for the remaining guarantees or rewrite them as documented content constraints and define how they are checked. “Watched failing” also lacks a durable record location, so T6 is not independently auditable.

- severity: blocker — AC8 omits required assertions for guarantees in AC3–AC6, conflicting with Article 3
- severity: major — T3 permits unbounded reintroduction of removed fetch and planning behavior
- severity: major — AC3 has no closed inventory or falsifiable completeness test
- severity: major — T1 leaves three flag-contract decisions unresolved
- severity: major — AC6 and T5 conflict on null-tracker artifact durability
- severity: major — AC7 does not define task-to-acceptance mapping or test the refusal behavior
- severity: minor — T6 does not specify where watched-failure evidence is recorded

verdict: concerns
